title: Electric Charges, Fields & Gauss's Law
subtitle: Zero-to-JEE-Advanced Visual Textbook: Charge Properties, Coulomb's Law, Superposition, Electric Field of Continuous Bodies (Rod, Arc, Ring, Disk), Electric Dipole Dynamics, Electric Flux & Gauss's Law Symmetry Applications
introduction:
💡 First-Time Reader Intuition: Welcome to Class 12 Electrodynamics!

In Class 11 (Gravitation), we saw that every particle has Mass ($m$), attracting other masses with $F = \frac{Gm_1 m_2}{r^2}$. Nature also possesses a second, vastly stronger intrinsic property called Electric Charge ($q$). Between two protons, the electrostatic repulsion is $10^{36}$ times stronger than gravity!

The 3 Branches of Electrodynamics:
  • 1. Stationary Charge ($v = 0$): Produces ONLY an Electric Field ($\vec{E}$).
  • 2. Constant-Velocity Charge ($\vec{v} = \text{const}$): Produces BOTH an Electric Field ($\vec{E}$) and a Magnetic Field ($\vec{B}$).
  • 3. Accelerating Charge ($\vec{a} \neq 0$): Produces $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ AND radiates Electromagnetic Waves!

topics.title: Properties of Charge, Coulomb's Law, Dielectric Mediums & Equilibrium of Point Charges
topics.theoryHtml:
1.1 Fundamental Properties of Charge & Coulomb's Law
  • 1. Quantization of Charge: $\boxed{q = \pm n e}$, where $e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}$ ($1\text{ C} \approx 6.25 \times 10^{18}$ electrons).
  • 2. Conservation of Charge: Total net charge in an isolated system is strictly conserved.
  • 3. Relativistic Invariance: Charge $q$ does not change with speed $v$ (unlike relativistic mass).
$$\text{Coulomb's Law in Vacuum & Medium }(K = \varepsilon_r): \qquad \boxed{F = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K}\frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2} = \frac{k}{K}\frac{|q_1 q_2|}{r^2}} \qquad \left(k = 9 \times 10^9\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{C}^2\right)$$
$$\text{Vector Form:} \qquad \boxed{\vec{F}_{21} = \frac{k q_1 q_2}{|\vec{r}_2 - \vec{r}_1|^3}(\vec{r}_2 - \vec{r}_1)}$$
1.2 Null Point & Three-Charge Equilibrium

For two like charges $+q_1$ and $+q_2$ separated by distance $d$, the null point (where a third charge $Q$ feels zero net force) lies between them at distance $x$ from $q_1$:

$$\boxed{x = \frac{\sqrt{|q_1|}}{\sqrt{|q_1|} + \sqrt{|q_2|}}\,d} \qquad \text{and for all 3 charges to be in free equilibrium:} \quad \boxed{Q = -\frac{q_1 q_2}{(\sqrt{q_1} + \sqrt{q_2})^2}}$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Suspended Pith-Ball Pendulums in Equilibrium: tan θ = F_e / (mg)

When two charged balls of masses $m_1, m_2$ and charges $q_1, q_2$ hang from a common point by threads of length $L$, both experience the exact same horizontal Coulomb repulsion $F_e = \frac{kq_1 q_2}{r^2}$. Balancing $T\sin\theta = F_e$ and $T\cos\theta = mg$ gives $\boxed{\tan\theta_1 = \frac{F_e}{m_1 g}}$ and $\boxed{\tan\theta_2 = \frac{F_e}{m_2 g}}$. Thus $\theta_1 = \theta_2$ if and only if $m_1 = m_2$!

topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: Dividing a charge $Q_0$ into two parts $q$ and $(Q_0 - q)$ gives maximum Coulomb repulsion when split into two equal halves ($q = Q_0/2$).

topics.title: Electric Field of Continuous Charge Distributions: Rod, Infinite Wire, Circular Arc, Ring & Disk
topics.theoryHtml:
2.1 Master Electric Field Dictionary
Charged BodyPoint LocationElectric Field Formula
1. Finite Straight Wire (Density $\lambda$)Perpendicular distance $r$$$E_{\perp} = \frac{k\lambda}{r}(\sin\theta_1 + \sin\theta_2), \quad E_{\parallel} = \frac{k\lambda}{r}(\cos\theta_2 - \cos\theta_1)$$
2. Infinite Straight Wire ($\theta_1 = \theta_2 = 90^\circ$)Distance $r$$$\boxed{E = \frac{2k\lambda}{r} = \frac{\lambda}{2\pi\varepsilon_0 r}}$$
3. Uniform Circular Arc (Angle $\alpha$, radius $R$)At center $O$$$\boxed{E = \frac{2k\lambda}{R}\sin\left(\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)}$$
4. Uniformly Charged Ring ($Q$, radius $R$)On axis at distance $x$$$\boxed{E(x) = \frac{k Q x}{(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}} \qquad \left(\text{Max at } \boxed{x = \pm\frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}}\right)$$
5. Uniformly Charged Disk ($\sigma$, radius $R$)On axis at distance $x$$$\boxed{E(x) = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(1 - \frac{x}{\sqrt{R^2 + x^2}}\right)}$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Calculus Derivation of Ring Axial Field & Maximum at x = ±R/√2

Integrating axial components $dE\cos\theta = \frac{k\,dq}{R^2+x^2}\frac{x}{\sqrt{R^2+x^2}}$ around the ring gives $E(x) = \frac{kQx}{(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}}$. Setting $\frac{dE}{dx} = 0$ yields $(R^2+x^2) - 3x^2 = 0 \implies x = \pm\frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}$, where $E_{\max} = \frac{2kQ}{3\sqrt{3}R^2}$.

topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: For $x \ll R$ near the center of a charged ring $+Q$, $E(x) \approx \frac{kQx}{R^3}$, so a test charge $-q$ (mass $m$) oscillates in SHM with time period $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{mR^3}{kQq}}$.

topics.title: Electric Dipole: Axial, Equatorial & General Field, Torque & Potential Energy in External Field
topics.theoryHtml:
3.1 Electric Dipole Moment ($\vec{p} = q(2\vec{a})$, Directed from $-q$ to $+q$)
$$\text{1. Axial Field:} \quad \boxed{\vec{E}_{\text{axial}} = \frac{2k\vec{p}}{r^3}} \qquad \bigg| \qquad \text{2. Equatorial Field:} \quad \boxed{\vec{E}_{\text{eq}} = -\frac{k\vec{p}}{r^3}} \qquad \bigg| \qquad \text{3. General:} \quad \boxed{E = \frac{kp}{r^3}\sqrt{3\cos^2\theta + 1}}$$
$$\text{Torque in Uniform } \vec{E}: \quad \boxed{\vec{\tau} = \vec{p} \times \vec{E}} \qquad \bigg| \qquad \text{Potential Energy:} \quad \boxed{U(\theta) = -\vec{p}\cdot\vec{E} = -pE\cos\theta}$$
$$\text{Work Done in Rotating from } \theta_1 \text{ to } \theta_2: \quad \boxed{W_{\text{ext}} = pE(\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2)} \qquad \bigg| \qquad \text{Angular SHM Period:} \quad \boxed{T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{I}{pE}}}$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Derivation of Axial vs. Equatorial Dipole Field

On the axial line at distance $r \gg a$, $E_{\text{axial}} = kq\left[\frac{1}{(r-a)^2} - \frac{1}{(r+a)^2}\right] = \frac{kq(4ra)}{(r^2-a^2)^2} \approx \frac{2kp}{r^3}$. On the equatorial line, horizontal components add to $E_{\text{eq}} = 2\left(\frac{kq}{r^2+a^2}\right)\frac{a}{\sqrt{r^2+a^2}} \approx \frac{kp}{r^3}$ opposite to $\vec{p}$.
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 185' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='185' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><text x='340' y='75' fill='#00e676' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>Dipole Fields: E_axial = 2kp / r³ (Parallel to p)   |   E_eq = −kp / r³ (Antiparallel to p)</text><text x='340' y='125' fill='#ffab00' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle'>Stable Equilibrium: θ = 0° (U = −pE)   |   Unstable Equilibrium: θ = 180° (U = +pE)</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: Work required to rotate a dipole from stable equilibrium ($\theta = 0^\circ$) to unstable equilibrium ($\theta = 180^\circ$) is $\mathbf{+2pE}$, whereas rotating from $0^\circ$ to $90^\circ$ requires $+pE$.

topics.title: Electric Flux, Gauss's Law, Cube Flux Shortcuts & Spherical/Cylindrical/Planar Fields
topics.theoryHtml:
4.1 Gauss's Law & Symmetry Applications
$$\boxed{\Phi_E = \oint \vec{E}\cdot d\vec{A} = \frac{q_{\text{enclosed}}}{\varepsilon_0}}$$
Symmetric SystemField / Flux Formula
1. Cube Flux Shortcuts (Point Charge $q$)Center of cube: $\frac{q}{6\varepsilon_0}$ per face; Corner of cube: $\frac{q}{8\varepsilon_0}$ total ($\frac{q}{24\varepsilon_0}$ through each of the 3 far faces).
2. Infinite Non-Conducting Sheet vs. ConductorInfinite sheet: $\boxed{E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}}$; Just outside conductor surface: $\boxed{E = \frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}}$.
3. Hollow Shell / Conducting Sphere ($Q, R$)Inside ($r < R$): $\boxed{E_{\text{in}} = 0}$; Outside ($r \ge R$): $\boxed{E_{\text{out}} = \frac{kQ}{r^2}}$.
4. Solid Non-Conducting Sphere ($Q, R, \rho$)Inside ($r < R$): $\boxed{\vec{E}_{\text{in}} = \frac{kQ}{R^3}\vec{r} = \frac{\rho}{3\varepsilon_0}\vec{r}}$; Outside: $E_{\text{out}} = \frac{kQ}{r^2}$.
5. Spherical Cavity Inside Solid Sphere ($\vec{d} = \vec{O_1 O_2}$)Uniform field everywhere inside cavity: $$\boxed{\vec{E}_{\text{cavity}} = \frac{\rho}{3\varepsilon_0}\vec{d}}$$
topics.derivationHtml:
Proof of Uniform Field Inside a Spherical Cavity

By superposition of a full sphere of density $+\rho$ centered at $O_1$ and a cavity sphere of density $-\rho$ centered at $O_2$, the field at any point $P$ inside the cavity is $\vec{E}_{\text{cavity}} = \frac{\rho}{3\varepsilon_0}\vec{r}_1 - \frac{\rho}{3\varepsilon_0}\vec{r}_2 = \boxed{\frac{\rho}{3\varepsilon_0}\vec{d}}$ (uniform!).
topics.graphSvg: <svg viewBox='0 0 680 185' style='width:100%;max-width:680px;height:auto;'><rect width='680' height='185' rx='8' fill='#080b12' stroke='#1e293b'/><text x='340' y='75' fill='#00f0ff' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' text-anchor='middle'>Hollow Shell: E_in = 0   |   Solid Non-Conducting Sphere: E_in = kQr/R³ = ρr/(3ε₀)</text><text x='340' y='125' fill='#00e676' font-size='12' text-anchor='middle'>Spherical Cavity Field: E_cavity = ρ d / (3ε₀) (Strictly Uniform Everywhere Inside Cavity!)</text></svg>
topics.jeeTraps: • Trap: Zero net flux ($\Phi_E = 0$) through a closed surface means $q_{\text{enclosed}} = 0$, NOT that $\vec{E} = 0$ at points on the surface!

conclusion: You have mastered Chapter 15: Electric Charges, Fields & Gauss's Law!
summary:
• Coulomb & Continuous Fields: $F = \frac{k|q_1 q_2|}{Kr^2}$; Wire $E = \frac{2k\lambda}{r}$; Ring $E = \frac{kQx}{(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}}$; Disk $E = \frac{\sigma}{2\varepsilon_0}\left(1 - \frac{x}{\sqrt{R^2+x^2}}\right)$.
  • Dipole & Gauss: $E_{\text{axial}} = \frac{2kp}{r^3}$, $E_{\text{eq}} = \frac{kp}{r^3}$; $\Phi = \frac{q_{\text{in}}}{\varepsilon_0}$; Cavity $E = \frac{\rho d}{3\varepsilon_0}$.
formulaSheetHtml:
ConceptMaster Formula
Charged Ring on Axis$E = \dfrac{kQx}{(R^2+x^2)^{3/2}} \quad (\text{Max at } x = \pm R/\sqrt{2})$
Dipole Torque & Energy$\vec{\tau} = \vec{p}\times\vec{E}, \qquad U = -\vec{p}\cdot\vec{E}$
Solid Sphere & Cavity$\vec{E}_{\text{in}} = \dfrac{\rho}{3\varepsilon_0}\vec{r}, \qquad \vec{E}_{\text{cavity}} = \dfrac{\rho}{3\varepsilon_0}\vec{d}$

questions.prompt: Two charges $+q$ and $+9q$ are separated by $40\text{ cm}$. At what distance from $+q$ does the net electric field vanish?
A charge $q$ is placed at one corner of a cube. What is the flux through any one of the three faces not touching the charge?
questions.explanation: Total flux through the cube is $\frac{q}{8\varepsilon_0}$, shared equally by the $3$ non-touching faces: $\frac{q}{24\varepsilon_0}$.

questions.prompt: A spherical cavity is carved inside a uniformly charged non-conducting sphere of density $\rho$ with center-to-center distance $d$. What is the electric field inside the cavity?
questions.explanation: By superposition, $\vec{E}_{\text{cavity}} = \frac{\rho}{3\varepsilon_0}\vec{d}$ is strictly uniform everywhere inside the cavity.
